title: The top capabilities technical teams need from a visual collaboration solution
summary: It can be tricky for tech teams to figure out which visual collaboration solution they need. Check out our guide for the best capabilities to look for.
body_markdown:
## Key takeaways


-


Choose an all-in-one visual collaboration solution that supports a wide range of use cases while serving both technical and non-technical teams.


-


Maximize productivity and eliminate context switching by selecting a platform with robust integrations and AI capabilities.


-


Boost technical innovation and efficiency with intelligent diagramming capabilities, including data linking, conditional formatting, and dynamic shapes.


-


A visual collaboration solution should streamline team alignment and act as a single source of truth, making it easier for cross-functional teams to share documents and understand complex workflows.


With so many


[visual collaboration](https://lucid.co/blog/what-is-visual-collaboration-definitions-and-examples) solutions on the market, it can be tricky to figure out which is the best option for your situation, especially if you work on a technical team. Team members in departments like engineering and IT have much different needs and more complex use cases for a visual collaboration platform than team members in, say, HR.


However, it doesn’t make sense to get different visual collaboration platforms for different departments. In order to


[consolidate your tech stack](https://lucid.co/blog/tech-stack-consolidation) , make it easy to share diagrams and other documents between teams, and ensure


[cross-functional collaboration](https://lucid.co/blog/cross-functional-collaboration-guide) , you need a visual collaboration solution that can support your entire business.


In fact, the solution you choose plays a large role in how productive, efficient, and innovative your organization is throughout the entire project lifecycle, from ideation to launch. This blog will provide you with a list of criteria to help you find a visual collaboration platform that supports your tech departments while also enhancing innovation and teamwork across your whole organization.


## The best visual collaboration features for technical teams


These are the top capabilities to keep in mind when evaluating visual collaboration platforms for your company and accommodating your technical teams.


These are the top capabilities technical teams need in a visual collaboration platform.


### Support of a wide range of use cases


Technical teams don’t work in silos; they collaborate closely with other teams. This means that your visual collaboration platform should be an all-in-one solution that supports the needs of your entire business—intelligent enough to handle complex diagramming for technical teams yet intuitive enough for other departments, such as marketing.


To make sure your visual collaboration solution is exactly what you need, look for a platform that not only supports ideation and meetings but also has the capability for complex use cases such as:


-


[Product roadmaps](https://lucid.co/blog/lucid-for-product-roadmapping) to show the status of epics and which teams are working on which ones.


-


[Dependency mapping](https://lucid.co/blog/how-to-use-dependency-mapping-to-boost-team-agility) to visualize project interdependencies and help you identify or mitigate risks.


-


[Capacity planning](https://lucid.co/blog/capacity-planning) and


[scenario planning](https://lucid.co/blog/business-scenario-planning) to estimate team workload and factor potential scenarios into strategy sessions.


-


Organizational charts to visualize and structure a variety of teams, from your entire tech department to


[Scrum teams](https://lucid.co/blog/how-Lucid-engineers-use-Lucid) .


-


[Wireframing](https://lucid.co/templates/wireframe) to visualize the layout of website and mobile pages and ensure a positive user experience.


-


[Entity relationship diagrams (ERDs)](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/16471565238292-Create-an-Entity-Relationship-Diagram-in-Lucidchart?anonId=0.1ecfb24a19ef1299e93&sessionDate=2026-08-05T00%3A49%3A11.234Z&sessionId=0.07dcbcb19fceca3546) , such as database diagrams, to illustrate how entities relate to each other within a system.


Use Lucid’s ERD templates to design or debug relational databases. Click on the image to get started.[Click on the image to use the template.](https://lucid.co/templates/entity-relationship-diagram-example-uml-notation)


### Intelligent diagramming capabilities


There’s a difference between


[diagramming software](https://lucid.co/blog/good-vs-great-diagramming-software) that’s “good enough” and diagramming software that’s great. You need a visual collaboration solution that goes beyond basic boxes and arrows, providing intelligent, next-generation diagramming capabilities to boost technical innovation and efficiency.


[Intelligence matters in visual collaboration](https://lucid.co/blog/most-intelligent-visual-collaboration-solution) because it makes data more accessible across your entire organization by turning that data into easy-to-understand visuals. For tech teams, intelligent diagramming software is particularly helpful for communicating cross-functionally and achieving clarity with stakeholders such as executives.


As you’re evaluating visual collaboration solutions, look for one that has intelligent diagramming features such as:


-


**Custom shape libraries,** so your team can create shapes and diagrams that are unique to the data you’re using, or you can tweak shapes to be exactly what you need for your team.


-


**The ability to automatically generate diagrams,** such as


[org charts](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/16463330693268-Create-an-org-chart?anonId=0.1ecfb24a19ef1299e93&sessionDate=2026-08-05T00%3A49%3A11.234Z&sessionId=0.07dcbcb19fceca3546) , from outside sources. With intelligent diagramming, you can import data sets from a variety of sources, like CSV or Excel files. From there, you can customize fields and even add pictures to easily visualize diagrams.


-


**Data linking.**


[Connecting to live data](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/16493391394068-Link-data-to-a-Lucidchart-document?anonId=0.1ecfb24a19ef1299e93&sessionDate=2026-08-05T00%3A49%3A11.234Z&sessionId=0.07dcbcb19fceca3546) creates dynamic visuals—not static ones—that update in real time, sparing your technical teams from providing manual updates.


-


**Conditional formatting and other automation features.** With features such as


[conditional formatting](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/16293796201108-Add-conditional-formatting-in-Lucidchart?anonId=0.1ecfb24a19ef1299e93&sessionDate=2026-08-05T00%3A49%3A11.234Z&sessionId=0.07dcbcb19fceca3546) ,


[dynamic shapes](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/14698910896532-Visualize-data-with-dynamic-shapes?anonId=0.1ecfb24a19ef1299e93&sessionDate=2026-08-05T00%3A49%3A11.234Z&sessionId=0.07dcbcb19fceca3546) , and


[smart containers](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/14690463943572-Visualize-data-with-Smart-Containers?anonId=0.1ecfb24a19ef1299e93&sessionDate=2026-08-05T00%3A49%3A11.234Z&sessionId=0.07dcbcb19fceca3546) , it’s possible to quickly evaluate data through visuals and gauge details or attributes, enhancing understanding.


-


**Features that automatically organize** your canvas, such as a


[grid layout](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/34727996594324-Use-assisted-layout-to-organize-content-in-Lucid?anonId=0.1ecfb24a19ef1299e93&sessionDate=2026-07-08T22%3A49%3A46.166Z&sessionId=0.a8d5850519f43d6a2e2) that intuitively arranges shapes and lines automatically, so your document looks professional and polished.


Intelligent features take your technical diagrams to the next level while enhancing clarity.[Learn more](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/34727996594324-Use-grid-layout-to-organize-content-in-Lucid)


### AI capabilities for collaboration and technical work


AI is


[transforming the way we work](https://lucid.co/blog/ai-solutions-for-business-challenges) and collaborate. By finding a visual collaboration solution that includes artificial intelligence capabilities, you can not only use AI to quickly create technical diagrams, but you can also use it to enhance collaboration in general with your teammates.


AI tools help you create visuals, kick off projects,


[improve processes](https://lucid.co/resources/webinars/ai-showcase-august-2024) , and brainstorm to come up with the best ideas. They eliminate a lot of manual work, freeing time for your tech team to focus on what’s most important.


Look for a visual collaboration solution that includes AI capabilities to help your teams:


-


**Generate and iterate** on diagrams in seconds. With


[Lucid AI](https://lucid.co/platform/ai) , for example, tech teams can generate visuals and documentation from text prompts, then tailor the output to their needs. You can even use Lucid AI to create conditional formatting rules for quick insights.


-


**Collaborate and ideate.** Look for AI capabilities that allow you to generate ideas, explore divergent thinking, and identify innovative solutions at lightning speed.


-


**Synthesize and summarize** essential work. For example, Lucid’s AI capabilities allow you to summarize Lucid documents directly


[in Slack,](https://lucid.co/marketplace/16c616de/slack) so you get a quick overview of your boards.


-


**Build and refine process diagrams.** The best solutions will not only accelerate process diagramming but also help you capture complete context. For example, with Lucid AI’s


[Process Agent](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/46461638983316-Use-the-Process-Agent-to-build-complex-diagrams-faster-with-Lucid-AI) , teams can build and refine complex diagrams faster through intelligent, clarifying questions. And with


[Process Capture](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/49874443096980-Use-Process-Capture-to-turn-screen-recordings-into-diagrams-with-Lucid-AI) , tech teams can generate process diagrams by recording their screen as they walk through a workflow. You can redact sensitive information before a diagram and associated SOP are generated.


Technical teams can quickly create complex diagrams with Lucid’s Process Agent.


### Easy document sharing and centralization


You need a


[visual collaboration](https://lucid.co/collaboration/online-collaboration-software) solution that not only provides a wide range of use cases for technical projects but also enables you to build a document repository and share your technical work with collaborators easily. This capability saves teams time from having to search for information or continually follow up with coworkers. Instead, team members can focus on important tasks and collaborate efficiently across functions on technical diagrams.


Look for a cloud-native visual collaboration solution that allows users to share and edit diagrams simultaneously without any extra steps, whether they’re inside your organization or outside of it.


Your visual collaboration solution should enable you to:


-


**Have**


[options for sharing documents](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/4642423138196-Share-with-collaborators-in-Lucid?anonId=0.1ecfb24a19ef1299e93&sessionDate=2026-08-05T00%3A49%3A11.234Z&sessionId=0.07dcbcb19fceca3546) **.** Seamlessly collaborate on your terms without compromising security by choosing—choose from a variety of sharing options, including password protection, expiring links, and unique Join IDs.


-


**Share your diagrams with collaborators outside of your organization** . A feature for inviting


[guest collaborators](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/13592910415380-Guest-Collaborators-in-Lucid?anonId=0.1ecfb24a19ef1299e93&sessionDate=2026-08-05T00%3A49%3A11.234Z&sessionId=0.07dcbcb19fceca3546) is highly beneficial when you need stakeholder input.


-


**Create a**


[single source of truth](https://lucid.co/blog/single-source-of-truth-guide) (SSOT) that’s a one-stop shop for teams to access data, documents, and information. This SSOT saves people time from having to locate documents or follow up with coworkers on their own. Look for the capability to bring in documentation from outside sources with options to either embed diagrams in existing documentation tools (such as


[Confluence](https://lucid.co/marketplace/b74196eb/confluence-cloud-embedded-links) ) or embed documentation alongside diagrams.


-


**Create official repositories** to centralize and share documents. Look for a solution that streamlines approval flows, strengthens governance, and enhances standardization by keeping official documentation in


[accessible repositories](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/38403665921684-Process-Accelerator-overview) .


In Lucid, you can create a shared, centralized space where team members can find all the documents they need, see updates, and make decisions together. Use features like[team hubs](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/25934104002324-Use-team-hubs-in-Lucid-to-collaborate-and-stay-organized) and team spaces to keep everyone organized and aligned on your work—technical or otherwise.


Team spaces in Lucid help you share documents and create a single source of truth for your team.


### Enhanced collaboration capabilities


A complete visual collaboration solution doesn’t just provide enhanced diagramming capabilities and a way to share documents. A great solution should also have built-in tools to help you collaborate more effectively with team members in the first place.


When we say visual collaboration, we mean using visuals to communicate ideas, solve complex problems, make decisions, and align on processes. It’s so much more than just cursors on a virtual whiteboard at the same time; a complete visual collaboration solution should include tools that support both live and


[asynchronous collaboration](https://lucid.co/blog/asynchronous-collaboration-guide) . This way, people can make contributions in real time and on their own.


Look for a solution that includes both synchronous and asynchronous features, such as:


-


**Features that enhance live facilitation.** For example, Lucid offers comprehensive templates that guide you through events such as a


[daily standup](https://lucid.co/templates/agile-daily-standup?p=1) or


[sprint retrospective](https://lucid.co/templates/sprint-retrospective-example?p=1) with embedded


[facilitation tools](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/25694707844628-Use-quick-tools-in-Lucid?anonId=0.1ecfb24a19ef1299e93&sessionDate=2026-08-05T00%3A49%3A11.234Z&sessionId=0.07dcbcb19fceca3546) that improve the experience for both contributors and facilitators.


-


**Features to guide collaborators** through a document and enhance understanding, such as


[frames and paths](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/14877877180564-Organize-content-with-Frames-in-Lucidspark) to follow along. This is especially helpful if people missed a live meeting and are exploring a document on their own time.


-


**Synthesis features** that help teams move on to planning after they’ve completed ideation stages. In Lucid, you can use


[Tags](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/14970913626516-Add-a-Tag-to-an-object-in-Lucidspark?anonId=0.1ecfb24a19ef1299e93&sessionDate=2026-08-05T00%3A49%3A11.234Z&sessionId=0.07dcbcb19fceca3546) to label and organize content, making it easier to categorize ideas or highlight important information.


-


**Decision-making features,** such as interactive activities, that help teams both capture and analyze input from all collaborators to make data-backed decisions.


-


**Features that enable anonymity** so people feel more comfortable making contributions. For example, you can brainstorm in


[private mode](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/26777352301460-Brainstorm-with-private-mode-in-Lucidspark?anonId=0.1ecfb24a19ef1299e93&sessionDate=2026-08-05T00%3A49%3A11.234Z&sessionId=0.07dcbcb19fceca3546) in Lucid to keep the names of collaborators hidden, even after the brainstorming session is over, encouraging


[psychological safety](https://lucid.co/blog/how-to-create-psychological-safety-at-work) among your teams.


It’s important to use a visual collaboration solution that captures all voices on your team and facilitates meaningful discussion. This drives innovation and decision-making. Lucid uniquely has


[Visual Activities](https://lucid.co/blog/visual-activities-use-cases) , which are a great tool for leading planning sessions, gathering feedback, capturing team morale, and


[building consensus](https://lucid.co/blog/team-consensus-building-techniques) .


Use Visual Activities in Lucid to empower your team to make decisions and prioritize tasks.[Try Visual Activities today with your team and dramatically improve your approach to collaboration. Click on the image to get started.](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/13893815605268-Collaborate-in-Lucid)


### Integrations with other tools you already use


Ideally, the visual collaboration solution you use is an all-in-one solution, which means that integration capability is a major factor. Technical teams, in particular, have essential tools they already use every single day, such as Jira and Azure DevOps. Look for a platform that offers tech-specific integrations for use cases such as


[enterprise architecture](https://lucid.co/blog/enterprise-architecture-repository) , user authentication and authorization, and cloud infrastructure visualization.


By choosing a visual collaboration solution with a


[depth of integrations](https://lucid.co/blog/lucid-integrations-guide) and automatic syncing capabilities, you can help your tech teams:


-


**Create a visual front-end for project management** that automatically synchronizes with existing systems of record, such as


[Jira](https://lucid.co/marketplace/488c820a/jira-embed) ,


[Azure DevOps](https://lucid.co/marketplace/eb5963d8/lucid-cards-for-azure-dev-ops-cloud) ,


[Atlassian](https://lucid.co/marketplace/atlassian) , or


[SmartSheet](https://lucid.co/marketplace/5d20313d/lucid-cards-for-smartsheet) . According to the most recent Gartner® Market Guide for Visual Collaboration Applications, “\[Bidirectional integrations\] can significantly reduce context switching, aiding productivity, and potentially allowing workflows that normally span several applications to be carried out using the visual collaboration application alone” (Gartner, “Gartner Market Guide for Visual Collaboration Applications,” October 27, 2025).


-


**Visualize technical infrastructure.** Get enterprise architecture insights with


[Ardoq](https://lucid.co/marketplace/8836527a/ardoq) and


[LeanIX](https://lucid.co/marketplace/94125ade/sap-lean-ix) integrations, and visualize your cloud environment across


[AWS](https://lucid.co/marketplace/91074b9b/aws) ,


[Azure](https://lucid.co/marketplace/ee0fb211/azure) , and


[Google Cloud](https://lucid.co/marketplace/2489d5df/google-cloud) .


-


**Streamline workflows** and add visual context through embedded


[Figma](https://lucid.co/marketplace/c6a75e22/figma) links.


-


**Connect with your AI ecosystem** by bridging visual context with your existing AI tools. Look for a solution that has an


[MCP server](https://lucid.co/marketplace/e16391cc/lucid-mcp-server) and connects with popular AI tools such as


[Claude](https://lucid.co/marketplace/b8a9e0ee/lucid-mcp-for-claude) ,


[Microsoft Copilot](https://lucid.co/marketplace/f184c9af/microsoft-copilot) , and


[ChatGPT](https://lucid.co/marketplace/f4db4a1f/ai-custom-gpt) .


Lucid’s integration with Jira features two-way syncing that automatically updates data in both platforms.[Learn more](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/14943046626964-Integrate-Lucid-Cards-with-Jira)


Lucid has an[integrations marketplace](https://lucid.co/marketplace) that offers dozens of integrations, from strategic planning and agile to options specifically for IT and engineering teams. With Lucid, you’ll get a wide range of integrations across leading ecosystems, such as Google and Microsoft, that contain fewer restrictions and provide customization that you won’t find anywhere else.


### Support services and implementation services


Once you select a visual collaboration solution, it isn’t as simple as just installing the program and having that be it. It takes time to learn a new platform. The right solution should offer continuous support, so you have all the resources you need to use the platform.


A visual collaboration solution should also be continually updated and improving over time, and it helps to have guidance on the newest features.


The best visual collaboration solution should include:


-


**Training on how to use the platform,** whether that’s live training provided by the platform’s team or


[online training tools.](https://training.lucid.co/?anonId=0.1ecfb24a19ef1299e93&sessionDate=2026-08-05T00%3A49%3A11.234Z&sessionId=0.07dcbcb19fceca3546)


-


**In-house**


[migration support](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us/articles/15178812313492-Import-files-into-Lucidspark?anonId=0.1ecfb24a19ef1299e93&sessionDate=2026-08-05T00%3A49%3A11.234Z&sessionId=0.07dcbcb19fceca3546) (both self-serve migration and white glove migration services) as you transition from other tools and begin using your new platform.


-


**Support for custom use cases,** so you can build customized templates and focus on what's most important for your business.


-


[Change management](https://lucid.co/blog/organizational-change-management-tips) **support.** It can be difficult to introduce a new collaboration solution to your organization, and change management services are a great way to receive guidance on implementing the platform so everyone quickly gets up to speed.


With an online


[help center](https://help.lucid.co/hc/en-us) and an entire team of dedicated customer success managers, Lucid has all the resources you need to successfully implement and maintain a new visual collaboration solution at your company. Lucid’s


[professional services team](https://lucid.co/professional-services) provides customized resources to help you use Lucid to achieve your organization’s goals.
